inputs.excerpt: financial results for its fiscal second quarter ended July 12, 2026.
inputs.claim: Q2 ends July 12, 2026; twelve subsequent weeks end October 4, 2026 (calendar calculation).

inputs.excerpt: In a 52-week fiscal year, the first fiscal quarter contains sixteen weeks and the second, third, and fourth fiscal quarters each contain twelve weeks.
inputs.claim: Fiscal third quarter contains twelve weeks; model period is July 13 through October 4, 2026.
Observed weekly sales-band statements were made August 11, within fiscal Q3.

inputs.excerpt: Tricia Tolivar: Yes. So it dipped initially to flat to positive and then each week sequentially got better and the last week was a mid-single-digit same restaurant sales.
inputs.claim: Partial fiscal-Q3 weekly observations: initially flat-to-positive, sequential recovery, latest observed week mid-single-digit; no exact weekly percentages or full-quarter average supplied.

inputs.excerpt: our same restaurant sales performance has recovered to mid-single digits.
inputs.claim: Latest observed weekly band in checked later-period searches remains this August 11 statement; projection requires assumptions for the remaining quarter.

method: I use fiscal Q3 July 13–October 4, twelve weeks after the cited July 12 Q2 end, and assume the August 11 comments summarize its first four completed weeks; initial flat-to-positive and latest mid-single-digit bands are subjective midpoints 1% and 5%, with a linear recovery averaging 3% across those four weeks. I assume the eight unobserved weeks average 5%, yielding (4*3+8*5)/12=4.333% and use a subjective normal quarterly standard deviation 1.5 percentage points for persistence, band interpretation, unequal sales weights and remaining-period uncertainty; this is a projection of observed weekly bands, not the full-year guidance. For a one-decimal reported percentage, P(reported > strike) uses a 0.05-point rounding correction; no later measured weekly band was verified in the checked sources, and report_date November 10 is expected/assumed rather than company-announced.
